title: Real-time Argo salinity was up to 0.004 too salty at 1000-2000 dbar in 2016-2022, but the RG grid did not keep this error and was fresher than adjusted floats after 2018 (2014-2026)
abstract: We compared real-time salinity, current delayed-mode adjusted salinity and the Roemmich-Gilson (RG) Argo grid at the same Argo profiles. We used all ascending core profiles on the 15th day of each month from January 2014 to September 2026 (50,642 open-ocean delayed-mode profiles) and converted the differences to a 0-2000 dbar halosteric sea-level equivalent. Real-time salinity with good real-time flags was too salty at 1000-2000 dbar by 0.0009 in 2014 and by 0.0043 (95% interval 0.0037-0.0048) in 2020; this equals a false halosteric fall of 1.2 mm and 6.2 mm. The share of profiles with a deep salty error of 0.01 or more rose from 8% to 18%. The RG grid did not keep this error: its deep difference from the adjusted floats stayed within plus or minus 0.0008. But the RG halosteric anomaly minus the float value changed from -1.5 mm in 2014-2017 to +1.6 mm in 2019-2024 (+2.3 to +3.5 mm in sensitivity tests), at the change from the RG base file to its near-real-time monthly files. Floats that needed no salinity correction show the same change. The adjusted floats show a halosteric fall of about 3 mm, mostly in the Atlantic at 100-700 dbar, that the RG grid and its global mean do not show. We cannot say if this fall is a real ocean change or an undetected sensor error. Limits: one day per month, a large backlog of profiles without delayed-mode checks after 2022, sample means that are not area-weighted, and no ship reference data. Code, aggregate tables, input hashes and figures are included; Argo and RG data stay external.

citations.reason: Found a false global salinity rise in gridded products that kept salty-drift data in 2015-2019. We confirm the size of the real-time error with matched profiles to 2026 and show that the RG grid does not keep it.
Linked post-2016 sea-level budget non-closure to Argo salinity; our halosteric differences quantify one part of this question for RG.
RG Argo climatology used as the gridded product under test.
Argo data modes and delayed-mode quality control.
Earlier campaign test of the RG grid against raw Argo for temperature; same RG files and profile-matching idea.
Raw Argo as a reference for gridded SST products; related use of raw versus adjusted Argo values.
Used RG salinity for a regional salt budget; our results give the size of RG salinity differences from adjusted floats after 2018.
